This position is responsible for the management, development, and delivery of afterschool garden education programming across three Auburn Union School District (AUSD) school garden sites. The role integrates garden stewardship, hands-on youth education, program coordination, and community partnership development.
Oversees ongoing care and upkeep of the garden to support program activities.
Garden Management & Stewardship:
Plans, develops, and delivers curriculum for youth, volunteers, and community members.
Oversees garden operations across three school sites, including seasonal planting and maintenance, soil health, irrigation, raised bed management, and garden improvement projects.
Recruits, trains, and manages volunteers in the garden.
Youth Education & Programming:
Actively participates in long-range strategic planning for the sites and programs.
Develops and delivers garden-based educational programming for youth enrolled in three afterschool programs in collaboration with AUSD expanded learning, education, and nutrition services staff.
Coordinates with garden activities with afterschool staff, teachers, and school nutrition services.
Volunteer Coordination & Community Engagement:
Evaluates and adjusts course curriculum through student/participant evaluations and the level of interest shown.

Coordinates monthly volunteer workdays, including outreach, recruitment, orientation, training, and on-site supervision. Develops and maintains relationships with volunteers, community partners, and county agencies to support program activities.
In collaboration with the school district, helps develop and track the budget for the garden program.
Partnership & Program Development:
Develops and maintains new and existing program partnerships.
Builds and maintains partnerships with classroom teachers, parent volunteers, and community organizations to expand school-community connections and strengthen garden education programming.
Facilitates and supports special program events in the garden.
Administrative Responsibilities:
Associate degree in related areas and/or equivalent experience.
Provides budget oversight and coordinates purchasing to support garden operations and program needs.
Continuing education in related field required.
This position is a career appointment that is 100% fixed.
Thorough knowledge of gardening, youth development, community engagement, and experience with horticulture and sustainable gardening practices
Thorough and effective verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills and presentation skills.
This job is open until filled. The first application review date will be 9/11/2026.
Thorough analytical skills to conduct analysis and develop recommendations, demonstrating organization and problem-solving skills.
Demonstrated skill in planning and developing new programs and curriculum and adjusting existing courses and curriculum in a continuing education environment.
Thorough knowledge of current community educational programs and trends.
Thorough knowledge in long-range strategic planning for community educational programs.
Demonstrated ability to recruit, train, and manage volunteers.
Thorough knowledge of organization policies and procedures.
Skill in using business software systems in the completion of work assignments, i.e., Word, Excel, Access, and PowerPoint.
Spanish language proficiency.
Special Conditions of Employment:
If working with youth: Must comply with regulatory agency reporting requirements (California's Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act).
